modifications: events[0].type changed from "snapshot" to "update" — both are documented values of that field, and the channel page states an update carries the trades of the last 250 ms.
sequence_num changed from 0 to 2, because every documented example prints 0 in isolation and a multi-frame scenario needs increasing values.
trades[0].trade_id changed from "000000000" to "000000001" so this is a different trade from the snapshot's.
trades[0].price changed from "1260.01" to "1260.02" and trades[0].time advanced, so the update is distinguishable.
trades[0].side changed from "BUY" to "SELL" — the other documented value — so the taker-side derivation is exercised in both directions.
A second trade was added to the same update, because the channel page states an update "can contain one or many trades".

The second trade's price and size are spelled "1260.030" and "1.50" — trailing fractional zeros. The venue types both fields as an unconstrained string and documents no canonical spelling, so an adapter must not assume one; this exercises the ADR-001 §3 normalization the boundary requires.

expectation: Parses. Produces two ReferenceTradeObserved events. The maker SELL yields takerSide BID; the maker BUY yields takerSide ASK. The second trade's price and size are canonicalized to "1260.03" and "1.5" before the domain boundary. Does not record a snapshot, because its type is "update".
